clue.text: Disrupt a program in authority

indicators.note: the first phrase sits inside the word for authority, so one piece is held within another

blocks.note: taken as written
a bot is a software program that runs automatically
a sage is a wise person consulted as an authority

explanation.surface: Someone in power wrecks a scheme or a broadcast from the inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'program' in the surface suggests a broadcast; here it is software, and bot is modern slang for an automated program.
explanation.definitionFit: To sabotage is to deliberately wreck or obstruct something, which is a forceful way to disrupt it.

clue.text: Accepts summer visitors

blocks.note: first meaning: takes in without protest, as of an insult or a tall story
second meaning: migratory birds that arrive in Britain for the warm months

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a host taking in holidaymakers; the visitors are birds that fly in for the summer.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means tolerates or believes uncritically, and the noun names the migratory birds that come north each summer.

clue.text: One keen on reading new work in progress rapidly

indicators.note: something new has been remade, so the letters of the following word come in a fresh order
the rearranged word sits inside the phrase that follows it

blocks.note: the four letters rearranged
to boom is to grow or prosper quickly

explanation.surface: Describes a reader who races through a fresh piece of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'progress rapidly' reads as part of the surface description of the reader, but it is the outer word that holds the shuffled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookworm is an avid reader, someone who loves books and always has one open.

clue.text: Notice, in play, fawn

indicators.note: one word is placed inside the other, as an actor is in a play

blocks.note: to toy with something is to play with it
a notice in a paper is an advert, AD for short

explanation.surface: Reads like a stage direction about a young deer appearing in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fawn' looks like the baby deer, but it is the verb meaning to flatter servilely.
explanation.definitionFit: To toady is to behave obsequiously to win favour, just as to fawn on someone is.

clue.text: Sheer roar going to shake one subjected to Beatlemania

indicators.note: shaking jumbles things up, so the preceding words are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: the fourteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Pictures the screaming of fans in the 1960s, loud enough to shake a pop star.
explanation.definitionFit: He was the Beatles' lead guitarist, so he was one of the four at the centre of the fan frenzy called Beatlemania.

clue.text: Mind tipsy cheers to some extent

indicators.note: only part of the following words is used, so the answer lies within them

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A drunken toast addles one's wits a little.
explanation.definitionFit: The psyche is the human soul or mind, the seat of thought and feeling.

clue.text: Odds on one ceremony being religious

blocks.note: SP is the starting price, the odds offered on a horse at the off
the Roman numeral for one
a ritual is a formal ceremony

explanation.surface: A betting tip placed on a single ceremony having a religious character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' simply strings the pieces together; SP is the betting abbreviation for starting price.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiritual means concerned with the soul and sacred matters, so it serves as an adjective for religious.

clue.text: Writer of music cut out? On the contrary

indicators.note: this tells the solver to swap the second word of the phrase for its opposite

blocks.note: to chop is to cut
the opposite of out

explanation.surface: Asks whether a composer's piece was removed from a programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut out' must become cut in, so CHOP + IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Frédéric Chopin was the Polish composer of piano music, so he is a writer of music.

clue.text: Attempts to rise in busy assembly

indicators.note: the answer is held within the following words rather than built from them
in a down clue, rising means reading the letters from bottom to top

blocks.note: the run of letters across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Efforts to get up and speak in a crowded meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: An essay is an attempt, the original sense of the word, so the plural matches attempts.

clue.text: Party win, then blundering on entrance? Not happy

indicators.note: a blundering effort is clumsy and muddled, so the words before it are jumbled

blocks.note: a do is a party
the seven letters rearranged
the mouth of a cave or river is its entrance

explanation.surface: A party wins, then stumbles at the door, and the mood sours.
explanation.definitionFit: Down in the mouth is an idiom for dejected, from the drooping corners of a sad face.

clue.text: Trouble after confusion getting rid of hard fruit

indicators.note: discarding something means a letter is dropped from the word for confusion

blocks.note: havoc is chaos and confusion
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
ado is fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: Confusion and trouble follow the disposal of some unripe fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hard' looks like it describes the fruit, but it names the letter to drop; H for hard is the pencil-grading convention.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocado is a pear-shaped tropical fruit with a large stone and buttery flesh.

clue.text: Threatening nothing, I'm retreating with common sense

indicators.note: something retreating goes backwards, so the letters before it run the other way

blocks.note: O looks like zero, nothing
taken as written
nous is British informal for practical good sense

explanation.surface: Someone threatening says they have nothing but are backing off sensibly.
explanation.definitionFit: Ominous means foreboding, suggesting that something bad is about to happen, as a threatening sky does.

clue.text: Artist, ironic, having look ahead

blocks.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold
wry humour is dry and ironic

explanation.surface: An artist with a sardonic outlook who sees what is coming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ahead' fixes the order of the two pieces. L. S. Lowry was an English painter of northern industrial scenes with matchstick figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Lowry is a famous painter, so the surname stands for an artist.

clue.text: Information list about island with unknown culture

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word wraps around the next piece

blocks.note: gen is British slang for information
a ship that lists leans, or tilts
I is the map abbreviation for island
in algebra x and y stand for unknowns

explanation.surface: A briefing list on an island's mysterious culture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'list' looks like a catalogue, but it is the verb to lean. I goes inside TILT, after the L.
explanation.definitionFit: Gentility is refinement and good manners, a sense of culture as polish rather than the arts.

clue.text: Promise controversy, repelled by awful fur on hood

indicators.note: something repelled is driven back, so the word before it runs backwards
an awful version is a mess, so the words after it are scrambled

blocks.note: a row is a heated dispute
the nine letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A fashion row in which someone recoils from a hideous fur-trimmed hood.
explanation.definitionFit: A word of honour is a solemn personal pledge, so it is a promise.

clue.text: Sensible to support parent, miles away, in different circumstances

indicators.note: the miles abbreviation goes away, so that letter is dropped from the parent

blocks.note: a mother is a parent
M is the abbreviation for miles
wise means sensible

explanation.surface: Advice that a sensible person would help a parent even when far from home.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'to support' puts WISE beneath the parent, so it comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: Otherwise is an adverb meaning if things were not so, which is the same as in different circumstances.

clue.text: Monarch in charge on hill breaking through

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so the first pieces go within the last

blocks.note: IC is the standard abbreviation for in charge
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor
via means by way of, through

explanation.surface: A queen in command on a hilltop forces her way through.
explanation.definitionFit: Victoria was the British queen who reigned from 1837 to 1901, so she is a monarch.

clue.text: Husband in pain not disposed to make response

indicators.note: the single letter is put inside the following words
disposed means arranged, so the letters are set out in a new order

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
the seven letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A husband in pain is not in the mood to reply.
explanation.definitionFit: An antiphon is a verse sung in response by a second choir in church music, a formal response.

clue.text: Seethe about scare by one with article in wartime leader's style

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word wraps around the rest

blocks.note: to churn is to seethe or boil up violently
a chill is a sudden fright
the Roman numeral for one
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A leader fumes over a wartime scare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seethe' looks like the leader's mood, but it is the outer word wrapped around the scare, the one and the article.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes rhetoric or defiance like that of Winston Churchill, Britain's prime minister during the Second World War.

clue.text: Working underground, initially dark

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word just before it

blocks.note: only the first letter is kept
sable is a poetic word for black or dark

explanation.surface: A miner at work below ground in the dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' could seem to apply to dark, but it belongs to underground.
explanation.definitionFit: Something usable is in working order, fit to be used.

clue.text: Problem in area raised hostility

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising the words means reading them from bottom to top

blocks.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
taken as written
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A dispute in a district has stirred up ill feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a container signal, but it is part of the reversed string.
explanation.definitionFit: Animus is ill will or animosity, a feeling of hostility toward someone.

clue.text: Working together in criminal ring, messy

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked, so the letters that follow are bent out of order

blocks.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A gang of crooks cooperates, but sloppily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'messy' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder; 'criminal' does that job.
explanation.definitionFit: Synergism is the combined action of parts producing an effect greater than each alone, so it means working together.

clue.text: All express annoyance with appeal overturned

indicators.note: something overturned is flipped, so the word before it is read the other way round

blocks.note: tut is the clicking sound of disapproval
it is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: Someone tuts in frustration when their appeal is rejected in court.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutti is the musical direction meaning all instruments or voices together.

clue.text: Connection that is found among sheep

indicators.note: being found among things means sitting inside them, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a tup is a ram
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A link uncovered within a flock.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie-up is a link or association, as between two companies, so a connection.

clue.text: Book with endless range, not at all for young child

indicators.note: without an end means the last letter is dropped from the word for range

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for book
an ambit is a scope or range
no means not at all

explanation.surface: A children's book with an endless scope is rejected outright.
explanation.definitionFit: Bambino is the Italian word for a baby or small child, used informally in English.

clue.text: Find university close to author's heart

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, so only the middle letters are kept

blocks.note: U is the abbreviation for university
near means close to
the middle two of six letters

explanation.surface: Someone at a university discovers what is closest to a writer's heart.
explanation.definitionFit: To unearth is to dig up or discover something hidden, so to find it.

clue.text: See art newly produced for festival

indicators.note: producing something anew means remaking it, so the letters are put in a fresh order

blocks.note: the six letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An invitation to view new artwork made for a festival.
explanation.definitionFit: Easter is the Christian festival celebrating the resurrection of Christ.

clue.text: Cleric taking tea, not elaborate

blocks.note: cha (or char) is British slang for tea
plain means simple, unadorned

explanation.surface: A vicar having a simple cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplain is a member of the clergy attached to a chapel, regiment, hospital or school.
